note: Ten cumulative tasks on the heartbeat service (PRD appendix A pilot). Each arm keeps the repository its own earlier tasks produced. Hidden tests live in benchmark/hidden/<task>/ and are never shown to the agent.

tasks.prompt: Bug: heartbeat.Validate accepts timestamps far in the future. It must reject a heartbeat whose At is more than 5 minutes after time.Now(); the error message must contain the word "future". Heartbeats at or before now+5m stay valid.

Add an HTTP endpoint GET /heartbeats/count that returns JSON {"count": N}, where N is the number of stored heartbeats. Change the constructor to api.NewServer(w kafka.Writer, counter interface{ Count() int }) and have cmd/heartbeat-worker pass the storage writer. Keep existing endpoints working.

Heartbeat payloads gain an optional integer field "version". Add `Version int` with JSON tag `version` to heartbeat.Heartbeat. heartbeat.Parse must set Version to 1 when the field is absent from the JSON.

storage.Writer must keep the full heartbeat including Version, and expose `func (w *Writer) Get(id string) (heartbeat.Heartbeat, bool)` returning the stored heartbeat. The INSERT statement must include the version column.

heartbeat.Consumer must retry store.Save on error, up to 3 attempts in total, waiting Consumer.Backoff between attempts (exported field `Backoff time.Duration`, default 100ms set by NewConsumer; tests set it to 0). After the third failure Handle returns an error that wraps the last Save error (errors.Is must work). A heartbeat saved after a retry is not deduplicated away on a later delivery of the same id... unless it was saved: an id counts as seen only after Save succeeded.
heartbeat.Consumer.Handle must be safe to call from many goroutines at once: when 100 goroutines deliver the same heartbeat id concurrently, the store must receive exactly one Save for it.

Refactor: move duplicate detection into a new package internal/dedupe with `type Set` and `func New() *Set` and method `func (s *Set) FirstSeen(id string) bool` (safe for concurrent use). heartbeat.Consumer must use it. Observable behavior of the consumer must not change.

POST /messages accepts an optional JSON integer field "priority" (0-9, default 0). A priority outside 0-9 is rejected with HTTP 400. The published Kafka message key becomes "<priority>:<key>" (for example "3:k").

Create package internal/config with `func HTTPAddr() string`: it returns env HTTP_ADDR, falling back to the old HEARTBEAT_HTTP_ADDR, falling back to ":8080". cmd/heartbeat-worker must use it instead of reading the environment itself.

Bug: heartbeat.Consumer.Run ignores context cancellation while the reader keeps returning messages. Run must return ctx.Err() promptly once the context is cancelled, even if messages are still available.
